compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090 (Blackwell): high SM count, large L2, fp16 tensor cores available; this workload is fp16 in/out but small enough to be bandwidth-bound. AvgPool 2x2 stride 2 halves spatial dims.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Conv 3x3 with C_in=16, C_out=32 is a small GEMM-like op per pixel (288 MACs); intensity is modest, memory traffic likely dominates.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: If we use fp16 with fp32 accumulate poorly, may lose accuracy; tensor cores need NHWC + multiples of 8.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input ~28MB fp16 (1*16*720*1280*2), output ~14MB (1*32*360*640*2). Weights ~9KB. Spatial reuse from 3x3 stencil; AvgPool reduces output writes 4x. Bandwidth bound regime.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Naive multi-kernel pipeline (conv->relu->pool) triples global traffic. Fusion is critical.

register_pressure.notes: Per-output-tile of 2x2 (pool window) over 32 out channels = manageable; weight reuse via shared memory.
register_pressure.risk: Spilling if we try to keep all 32 channels in registers per thread.

nodes.notes: 1) Classification: fused stencil + pointwise + reduction (Conv3x3 NCHW + ReLU + AvgPool2x2). Inputs fp16; weights/bias fp16; output fp16, shape [1,32,360,640]. 2) Math: y[n,oc,oh,ow]=avg_{i,j in 2x2}(relu(sum_{ic,ky,kx} W[oc,ic,ky,kx]*x[n,ic,2*oh+i+ky-1,2*ow+j+kx-1]+b[oc])). Per output pixel reduces over (ic=16,ky=3,kx=3)=144 macs plus 4-pixel pool avg => 576 macs/output. 3) Layout: NCHW fp16 contiguous. Weights tiny (32*16*9*2=9216 B) -> fit in shared/const. For one output pool pixel need a 4x4 region of conv outputs => 5x5 input footprint per (n,ic). Heavy spatial reuse. 4) Regimes: (a) memory-bound full image -> fusion + vectorized loads dominate; (b) small batch=1 -> need enough blocks to fill SMs across spatial tiles; (c) channel-parallel reductions across ic=16 (small) fit in one warp. 5) Knobs: fusion granularity (single fused kernel vs split), tile size (OH_tile x OW_tile per block), keep weights in shared/const, NCHW vs NHWC, fp16 math vs fp32 accumulate, vectorized half2/float4 loads, AvgPool merged via direct 4x4-input->1-output computation. 6) Skeleton: grid over (oc_tile, oh_tile, ow_tile, n). Each block loads weights to smem once, loads input tile (with halo) to smem, each thread computes one output pool pixel by summing 4 conv outputs each requiring 3x3*ic mac, with ReLU then /4. 7) Families: F1 Single fused kernel NCHW with shared-memory input tile + weights in smem (top candidate, full fusion fits: weights 9KB + input tile <16KB). F2 Implicit-GEMM style via tensor cores after NHWC layout transform (higher peak but layout overhead, batch=1 small). F3 Two-kernel: fused conv+relu writing to scratch then pool (baseline-ish, extra global traffic; rejected unless F1 fails). Pick F1.

action.description: Implement a single fused CUDA kernel performing Conv3x3(pad=1) + bias + ReLU + AvgPool2x2 in one pass. Grid maps blocks to (oc_block, oh_tile, ow_tile). Each block loads weights for its oc_block into shared memory once, cooperatively loads the corresponding input halo tile per ic across all ic into shared/registers, computes 2x2 conv outputs per output pool pixel, applies ReLU, averages, writes a single fp16 output. Use fp32 accumulators, fp16 loads via __half2.
action.rationale: Eliminates intermediate global traffic between conv/relu/pool; weights tiny so easily cached; spatial reuse via shared memory. Best fit for bandwidth-bound regime on RTX5090.
action.title: Fused NCHW Conv3x3+ReLU+AvgPool kernel with shared-mem weights+input tile

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: NCHW fp16, fp32 accumulators. No tensor cores but compute is light (~576 MACs/output) and easily handled by FFMA.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Good FMA reuse via 3x3 sliding window across 2x2 pool outputs.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Single global read of input per tile, single write of output; weights in constant cache.

register_pressure.notes: OC_CHUNK=8 with 4 outputs/thread and 16 p[][] floats may spill; __launch_bounds__(128,8) only achievable if regs<=32.

nodes.notes: CURRENT: Single fused NCHW kernel does Conv3x3+bias+ReLU+AvgPool2x2 in one pass; loads all 16 input channels of a 18x34 halo tile into shared mem, weights/bias in constant mem, each thread accumulates 4 conv outputs over 8-oc chunks then ReLU+avg. bottleneck: likely shared-memory bandwidth / register pressure (each thread holds OC_CHUNK*4=32 floats acc + 16 p[4][4] regs). FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent=yes. UPDATE_BELIEF: 6.40x speedup at 0.671ms vs 4.291ms ref confirms fusion + shmem tile is strong on RTX5090. Next bet: push further via vectorized __half2 IO + smaller per-thread output footprint to free regs and raise occupancy; or warp-level OC parallelism.

action.description: Transform input to NHWC, use WMMA/tensor cores to compute conv (im2col-implicit) at fp16, fuse ReLU and AvgPool in epilogue. Requires layout conversion of input/output around the kernel or a preface kernel.
action.rationale: Tensor cores give huge fp16 throughput, but problem is bandwidth-bound and tiny GEMM K=16*9=144 leaves tensor cores underutilized; layout conversion adds traffic.
action.title: NHWC tensor-core implicit-GEMM conv with fused ReLU+pool epilogue

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: WMMA requires multiples of 16/8 along M,N,K. K=144 ok, but C_in=16 small; M (out pixels) huge fine.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Compute peak is overkill; little benefit.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Layout swap adds reads/writes; may hurt vs F1.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Net regression if conversion isn't fused.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: mutually exclusive with n1/n3 (different layout+primitive). De-prioritized: n1 already 6.4x; WMMA on tiny C_in=16 with 3x3 conv has poor m/n/k alignment and large rewrite cost. Keep open as exploratory.

action.description: Two-kernel pipeline: kernel A fuses Conv3x3+bias+ReLU writing fp16 to a scratch buffer of size [1,32,720,1280]; kernel B reads it to do AvgPool2x2 to final [1,32,360,640]. Simpler but extra ~28MB round-trip.
action.rationale: Easy fallback that still fuses conv+relu; useful baseline for correctness and bandwidth comparison.
action.title: Two-kernel split: fused Conv+ReLU then AvgPool

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Standard NCHW conv kernel; no special HW use.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Adds intermediate read/write of full pre-pool tensor.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: exclusive with n1 (split kernels vs fused). Dominated by n1's 6.4x — splitting reintroduces intermediate global traffic. Strongly de-prioritized.

action.description: Under F1 fused kernel, choose tile size of OH_tile=8, OW_tile=16 output pool pixels per block (i.e., 16x32 conv-output pixels, plus halo 18x34 input pixels per ic). Block has 128 threads, each producing 1 pool-output across all 32 oc looped, or split oc into two halves (16+16). Weights staged to shared memory once per block.
action.rationale: Balances smem (~ 18*34*16*2 = ~19.5KB input tile + 9KB weights) and occupancy. Pool fusion saves halo redundancy.
action.title: Tune F1 occupancy: reduce OC_CHUNK & vectorize __half2 IO

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Need to verify register count <=64 for 2 blocks/SM.

memory_bandwidth.risk: Too large reduces block count -> SM underuse on small image (only 360*640/(8*16)=1800 blocks * oc_tiles, plenty).

register_pressure.notes: 32 oc accumulators per thread risky; may need oc loop or oc_tile=8/16.

nodes.notes: Map 32 OCs across 32 lanes of a warp; each lane owns 1 OC for a tile of 2x2 outputs, eliminating OC loop and slashing per-thread accumulator regs. action.title: Use __half2 FMA math + fp16 weights in shmem (skip fp32 constant)

nodes.notes: Keep weights as __half in constant/shmem and use __hfma2 across 2 outputs; halves memory and doubles math throughput. Risk: accuracy tolerance. SELF_CHECK: alternative refinement of n1, mutually exclusive with n1a/n1b as the next chosen step.

kernel_summary: Fused Conv2d(3x3, pad=1, C_in=16, C_out=32) + bias + ReLU + AvgPool2x2(stride 2) on fp16 NCHW input of shape [1,16,720,1280] producing [1,32,360,640]. Workload is small per output (~576 MACs) and memory-bound on RTX5090; weights tiny (~9KB) and easily kept in shared/constant memory. Best strategy is a single fused kernel that loads an input halo tile + weights to shared memory, computes conv with fp32 accumulators, applies ReLU, averages a 2x2 block, and writes one fp16 output—eliminating the intermediate full-resolution pre-pool tensor traffic. Key constraints: fp16 I/O with fp32 accumulate for accuracy (rtol/atol 0.01), NCHW layout fixed by reference, weights/bias provided via set_params, output shape and dtype must match reference exactly.
open_questions: Are the weights/bias stored as fp16 after .half() conversion, and what is the exact memory layout passed to set_params?
Does the reference cast to fp32 internally for accumulation, and what numerical tolerance margin does that give us?
Is AvgPool2x2 using count_include_pad=True/False semantics (border effects at H=720,W=1280 which are even, so no border issue here)?
What's the achievable DRAM bandwidth on RTX5090 in practice (HBM/GDDR7 ~1.8TB/s) — sets the floor on attainable latency (~24ms-input + 14MB-output / BW)?
Best block/tile shape balancing smem (input halo tile per block) vs occupancy and oc-loop unrolling?
Should we use __half2 vectorized loads along W to halve global load instructions for the input tile?
Is it worth a one-time layout transform to NHWC to enable tensor cores given the tiny K=144 GEMM?
Can constant memory or __ldg cache hold the 9KB weight tensor more efficiently than shared memory?
